items.title: Zelensky warns of possible departures from Kyiv ahead of winter
items.summary: In a BBC interview, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky acknowledged that residents could leave Kyiv amid Russian attacks. He also said US air-defence deliveries were being delayed and Ukraine faced a severe shortage of interceptors against ballistic missiles.

items.title: US and EU reportedly increasingly divided over Ukraine support
items.summary: Politico, citing sources, reported growing disagreements over continued support for Ukraine. Donald Trump reportedly questioned the effectiveness of billions of dollars in assistance during a November 19 conversation with Zelensky.

items.title: Russian-appointed Luhansk authorities increase war damage compensation
items.summary: The regional administration announced an increase in compensation for destroyed housing from 51,500 to 70,000 rubles per square metre. Payments for lost essential belongings will also rise, with recalculations applying to decisions made since August 8, 2026.

items.title: Russia extends aviation fuel export ban through March 2027
items.summary: The Russian government has extended its ban on exports of jet fuel until March 31, 2027.

items.title: Zelensky questioned over energy-sector corruption investigation
items.summary: In a BBC interview, Zelensky declined to directly identify a person referred to in recordings linked to an energy-sector corruption investigation. He said anti-corruption authorities had no questions for him and defended Ukraine's ongoing anti-corruption reforms.

items.title: Russia expands restrictions on collection of military-related information
items.summary: Russia's Justice Ministry has reportedly registered an FSB order expanding the list of sensitive but unclassified military information. The additions include information about recruitment of prisoners and criminal suspects, and private financial information concerning military personnel and defence industry workers. Collection on behalf of foreign interests may carry legal consequences.

items.title: Thousands of Donetsk electricity customers face outages
items.summary: The local electricity provider in Russian-occupied Donetsk reported that 40,500 customers remained without power, citing excessive network loads affecting several districts.

items.title: Russian authorities report civilian injuries following drone incidents
items.summary: Russian reports say a woman was hospitalized following a drone incident in St Petersburg. Regional governors also reported civilian injuries in Bryansk and Kursk regions. The reports have not been independently verified.

items.title: FSB claims it prevented assassination attempt in occupied Donetsk
items.summary: Russia's security service said it detained a woman accused of cooperating with Ukrainian intelligence in an alleged plot against a senior Russian serviceman. A treason investigation has been opened. The allegations have not been independently verified.

items.title: Zelensky criticizes Trump's friendly rhetoric toward Putin
items.summary: In a reported interview exchange, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky criticized Donald Trump's characterization of Vladimir Putin as a friend, arguing that Russia's aggression against Ukraine makes such a characterization unacceptable.

items.title: Russia claims 318 Ukrainian drones intercepted overnight
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said its air defences intercepted 318 Ukrainian drones overnight. The figure has not been independently verified.

items.title: Russian-installed court reports sentences against Ukrainian servicemen
items.summary: The supreme court in Russian-occupied Donetsk said 25 Ukrainian servicemen had been convicted since the beginning of the year, including six sentenced to life imprisonment. Some convictions were issued in absentia.

items.title: Hungary objects to proposed €100 billion EU aid allocation for Ukraine
items.summary: Hungarian Prime Minister Magyar said Hungary disagrees with the proposed volume of assistance for Ukraine in the EU budget, objecting to demands for increased support under centralized directives.

items.title: Ukrainian court reportedly orders discharge of unlawfully mobilized man
items.summary: A court in Poltava reportedly ruled a military medical commission's decision unlawful and ordered a man's discharge after six months of military service. His medical records were allegedly altered to make him eligible for mobilization.

items.title: Russia proposes seafood import duties of up to 35%
items.summary: Finance Minister Anton Siluanov said a proposal to impose duties of up to 35% on seafood from countries designated unfriendly by Moscow had been submitted to relevant government departments for coordination.

items.title: Energy and railway infrastructure reportedly damaged in Vinnytsia region
items.summary: Local authorities reportedly confirmed damage to energy and railway infrastructure following an attack in Ukraine's Vinnytsia region. Damage to critical infrastructure was also reported in Kirovohrad region.

items.title: Russian embassy warns of deteriorating relations with Moldova
items.summary: Russia's embassy in Chișinău reportedly warned of an unspecified possible provocation that could worsen bilateral relations. The warning follows Moldovan protests over alleged drone incursions and discussions of regional air-defense cooperation. Moscow disputes that the drones' origin was established.

items.title: Zelensky highlights shortage of air defence missiles
items.summary: Zelensky described Ukraine's air defence shortage as a major problem and criticized the prioritization of US missile supplies for Israel, according to a report of his remarks.

items.title: Finland reportedly holds major multinational military exercises
items.summary: Reports describe a series of Finnish military exercises involving approximately 25,000 participants from ten countries. The exercises reportedly include opportunities for defence companies to test new technologies, following Finnish-Ukrainian cooperation on unmanned systems.

items.title: Russia says processing times for military family benefits have halved
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry says digital services and administrative centres have reduced processing times for benefits for military personnel and their families. The ministry also reported introducing an automated telephone assistant to handle initial enquiries.

items.title: US reportedly delays review of military presence in Europe
items.summary: Politico reportedly says the Pentagon will not present its military posture review by the December NATO foreign ministers' meeting. European proposals to replace some American capabilities with their own reportedly contributed to the delay. No revised deadline has been announced.

items.title: Estonia calls for additional EU funding for eastern border states
items.summary: Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal reportedly called for additional funding for Estonia and other EU eastern border countries to address the consequences of Russia's war against Ukraine.

items.title: Serbia's acting president reportedly rejects sanctions against Russia
items.summary: Acting President Aleksandar Cupic reportedly said Serbia would not impose sanctions on Russia. The position comes amid uncertainty over expiring energy arrangements and Serbia's continued pursuit of EU membership.

items.title: AfD leader advocates negotiations with Moscow
items.summary: Alice Weidel reportedly called for direct German negotiations with Russia and argued that a peace agreement would require Ukrainian territorial concessions. Her remarks represent her party's position, not German government policy.

items.title: Russia delays jury trials in occupied Ukrainian regions until 2030
items.summary: Russia's Federation Council reportedly approved legislation postponing jury trials in Russian-occupied Ukrainian territories until January 1, 2030, citing organizational difficulties and concerns about the safety of trial participants.

items.title: Russia and Turkey extend gas supply contract for three years
items.summary: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said Gazprom and Turkey's Botas extended their gas supply agreement for three years on existing terms. He also said Novatek would begin supplying LNG to Turkey in January 2027.

items.title: Russia and Ukraine reunite 43 civilians with families
items.summary: A humanitarian operation at the Nova Huta crossing on the Belarus–Ukraine border reportedly enabled 20 people to travel from Ukraine to Russia and 23 in the opposite direction. Most participants were elderly.

items.title: Ukrainian newspaper alleges surveillance of its journalists
items.summary: Ukrainska Pravda editor-in-chief Sevgil Musaieva alleges that security service personnel followed journalists investigating parliamentary faction leader David Arakhamia. She has requested explanations from Arakhamia and the security service. The allegations have not been independently verified.

items.title: Prolonged water outages reported in Dnipro
items.summary: Local media reportedly say three districts have experienced five days without water supplies amid prolonged electricity disruptions. Residents have expressed concern about deteriorating humanitarian conditions.

items.title: Gazprom official warns of higher European gas prices
items.summary: Gazprom official Polous predicted that European gas prices could rise following the implementation of restrictions on Russian liquefied natural gas, warning of a possible repeat of the 2022 energy crisis. This is a company forecast rather than an established outcome.

items.title: Russia claims new territorial gains in weekly military update
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry claimed control of Sosnovy Bor in Kharkiv region and Barvinovka in Zaporizhzhia region in its November 21–27 update. The claims have not been independently verified.

items.title: Ukrainian anti-corruption chiefs discuss reform safeguards with EU commissioner
items.summary: Ukraine's anti-corruption agencies said their leaders met European Commissioner Valdis Dombrovskis in Brussels on November 26 to discuss institutional independence and reforms linked to EU budget support in 2027. Participants agreed on the importance of preventing reversals of anti-corruption reforms.

items.title: Broadcasting disrupted in Russian-occupied Rovenky
items.summary: Russian-appointed Luhansk leader Leonid Pasechnik said television broadcasting was completely disrupted and radio broadcasting partially interrupted following strikes he attributed to Ukrainian forces. The attribution has not been independently verified.

items.title: Kremlin says Putin and Pashinyan will discuss Russian military base
items.summary: Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said the Russian military base in Armenia would be discussed during upcoming talks between Vladimir Putin and Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan.

items.title: Russian-appointed Luhansk authorities report civilian casualties
items.summary: Leonid Pasechnik reported one civilian killed and three injured in incidents across occupied Luhansk region that he attributed to Ukrainian attacks. The accounts have not been independently confirmed.

items.title: Russian military bloggers report damage to Ukrainian banknote production facility
items.summary: Russian military bloggers reported renewed strikes affecting a banknote production facility in Malyn, Zhytomyr region. The extent of damage and the claims about the facility have not been independently verified.

items.title: Italy denies prior coordination over reported Ukrainian attack in Libya
items.summary: Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said Italy had not been informed of the operation, contradicting Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky's remarks about coordination with international partners. Former Italian Prime Minister Giuseppe Conte called for parliamentary clarification from the government.

items.title: Ukrainian appeals court upholds prison sentence in energy-related bribery case
items.summary: Ukraine's High Anti-Corruption Court upheld a four-and-a-half-year prison sentence for a lawyer convicted of offering prosecutors $200,000 to transfer an investigation involving alleged misappropriation of electricity and laundering of 716 million hryvnias. The court modified parts of the judgment while retaining the sentence.

items.title: Lavrov highlights expanding Russian trade with UAE
items.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said bilateral trade with the United Arab Emirates rose by 56% last year. He announced that the next meeting of the bilateral economic cooperation commission is scheduled for December 8 in Moscow.

items.title: Kursk police report rescuing two people after drone attack
items.summary: Regional police said officers rescued a man and a woman from a burning vehicle following an attack attributed to a Ukrainian drone and transported them to a medical facility.

items.title: Russia expands foreign-agent register
items.summary: Russia's Justice Ministry added media manager Yegor Kuroptev, human rights advocate Fatima Gazieva, activist Musa Lomaev, journalist Alexey Artyukh and the online publication Rabkor to its foreign-agent register. The ministry separately announced the removal of former Wikimedia Russia executive director Stanislav Kozlovsky.

items.title: Preferential reconstruction loans introduced in occupied Donetsk region
items.summary: The head of a Russian-appointed regional microcredit company said businesses affected by shelling have begun receiving reconstruction loans at an interest rate of 0.1%. He said the company had provided more than 230 million rubles in support to 73 small and medium-sized businesses this year.

items.title: Novorossiysk authorities report damage to 70 apartments following drone attack
items.summary: Regional emergency authorities reported damage to windows in 70 apartments following a drone attack on November 27. Municipal teams were assessing damage and assisting residents, while gas services had restored supply to two entrances of an affected apartment building.

items.title: Italian MEP criticizes proposed additional EU funding for Ukraine
items.summary: Italian European Parliament member Roberto Vannacci criticized further financial support for Ukraine during a parliamentary speech, arguing that European taxpayers would bear the cost of borrowing. He also criticized the European Commission's response to Ukrainian blacklisting of European politicians.

items.title: Crimean authorities expect electricity restrictions to end next week
items.summary: Russian-installed energy authorities in Crimea say electricity restrictions introduced on November 25 could be lifted by the end of next week. Repairs to generating facilities and high-voltage networks are continuing, with longer outages affecting some consumers.

items.title: EU military mobility plans reportedly target 2027
items.summary: A report on the November 25 meeting of EU military chiefs says discussions focused on reducing administrative and customs barriers to military transport by 2027, including arrangements for sharing transport resources and involving civilian logistics companies.

items.title: Putin attends commissioning ceremony for nuclear-powered submarine
items.summary: President Vladimir Putin attended the flag-raising ceremony for the Perm submarine in Severodvinsk. The Kremlin also announced a meeting on the development of Russia's multipurpose nuclear-powered submarine fleet.

items.title: Russian-installed Kherson governor reports civilian casualties
items.summary: Russian-installed governor Vladimir Saldo said 11 civilians were killed and 20 injured in attacks he attributed to Ukrainian forces over the past week. The figures have not been independently verified.

items.title: Moscow warns Latvia of possible diplomatic countermeasures
items.summary: Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova accused Latvia of escalating tensions with Russia, citing its military support for Ukraine, NATO exercises and restrictions on Russian grain transit. She warned that Moscow reserves the right to respond politically and diplomatically. Her allegations concerning Ukrainian drone operations were not independently verified.

items.title: Russia begins forming military construction units
items.summary: Deputy Defence Minister Pavel Fradkov reportedly announced the formation of military construction units staffed by conscripts and contract personnel. The initiative is intended to reduce reliance on commercial contractors for military infrastructure, with dedicated training arrangements planned.

items.title: Dnipro residents reportedly protest prolonged electricity outages
items.summary: Residents reportedly blocked a road in Dnipro to protest prolonged power cuts. One participant said their household had been without electricity for five days. The report illustrates mounting pressure on civilians amid disruptions to essential services.

items.title: Russia claims strikes on Ukrainian railway locomotives
items.summary: The Russian Defence Ministry said its forces struck three railway locomotives in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region, alleging they were used to transport military cargo. The claim has not been independently verified.

items.title: Ireland reportedly ends hotel accommodation for some Ukrainian refugees
items.summary: Irish authorities have reportedly ended hotel accommodation for Ukrainian refugees who arrived before March 2024. Some people unable to secure alternative housing have been relocated to converted equestrian facilities, prompting complaints about living conditions and a protest in Dublin.

items.title: Russia reports intercepting 74 Ukrainian drones during the day
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said its air defences intercepted 74 Ukrainian drones over Russian regions during the day. The figure has not been independently verified.

items.title: Iran disputes responsibility for deadly Kuwait incident and accuses Ukraine
items.summary: Iranian representatives alleged Ukrainian involvement in a deadly incident at a military facility in Kuwait. Kuwait and Italy attributed the incident to Iran, which denies responsibility. The Iranian allegation remains unverified.

items.title: Serbian filmmaker advocates feature films about the Donbas war
items.summary: Speaking at a documentary film festival in Serbia, director Emir Kusturica argued that fictional feature films based on experiences of people involved in the Donbas conflict should be produced.

items.title: Ukraine's household utility arrears reportedly exceed 101 billion hryvnias
items.summary: Figures attributed to Ukraine's state statistics service put outstanding utility payments above 101 billion hryvnias, including 16 billion for electricity and 11 billion for water and sewerage services.

items.title: Russian-appointed authorities report drone attack on ambulance
items.summary: The regional health ministry in Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia said an ambulance transporting a patient was attacked by a drone. It reported that the medical crew and patient escaped without injury. The account has not been independently verified.

items.title: Russia launches parliamentary training programme for war veterans
items.summary: A reported training initiative for 39 newly elected State Duma deputies who are veterans of the war in Ukraine focuses on legislative work, parliamentary oversight and communication with constituents.

items.title: Austria presents new counter-drone strategy
items.summary: Austria reportedly unveiled plans to strengthen drone oversight and counter-drone capabilities, including a proposed Interior Ministry coordination centre. Legislative changes are expected next year, while funding and operational responsibilities remain unresolved.

items.title: Zelensky reportedly acknowledges lack of consultation over Libya operation
items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky reportedly acknowledged that Kyiv did not consult international partners before the reported operation in Benghazi. The statement follows Italy's denial that it had been informed beforehand.

items.title: Britain and Sweden reportedly agree on missile supplies for Ukraine
items.summary: Britain and Sweden reportedly signed an agreement concerning air-to-air missile supplies for Ukraine's planned Gripen fighter fleet. Delivery timelines remain uncertain.

items.title: Russian military convoys reportedly turn back following Libya incident
items.summary: Reuters reportedly said two Russian military convoys bound for Libya turned back following a reported Ukrainian attack on a Russian naval vessel in Benghazi. The account has not been independently verified here.

items.title: Russian digital ministry reportedly unable to reach agreement with Apple
items.summary: Digital Development Minister Maksut Shadayev reportedly said talks with Apple over enabling 5G and restoring the MAX messaging app to its store had not produced results. Apple has reportedly not cooperated with Russian telecommunications operators since 2022.

items.title: Rheinmetall reportedly reconsidering Ukrainian ammunition factory
items.summary: Rheinmetall CEO Armin Papperger reportedly indicated that the company may abandon its planned ammunition production facility in Ukraine, citing a lack of progress over the past year. A final cancellation has not been confirmed.

items.title: Moscow mayor reports interception of 19 drones
items.summary: Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin reported that air defences intercepted 11 drones heading toward the capital, followed by another eight. The reported interceptions have not been independently verified.

items.title: Drone strikes reported in Kremenchuk and Dnipro
items.summary: Russian military bloggers reported drone strikes in Kremenchuk and explosions in Dnipro. The extent of damage and any casualties remain unconfirmed.

items.title: Russian authorities provide assistance to stranded Estonian border travellers
items.summary: Leningrad Region Governor Alexander Drozdenko said more than 50 Narva residents were stranded in freezing conditions at the border. Regional authorities provided a heated bus and assistance with accommodation amid reported delays at the Estonian checkpoint.
